statements.venue: Press release statement after voting for the Ratepayer Protection Act
statements.quote: The U.S. must remain globally competitive in the advancement of artificial intelligence, which requires supporting the infrastructure and energy resources necessary for this growing technology
statements.context: Crapo explained his vote to advance a bill making large data centers pay for the electricity infrastructure they need, rather than ratepayers.
statements.reason: The statement is about AI competitiveness and data center electricity costs and does not acknowledge any catastrophic risk from AI.

slowdown.note: No statement found for or against slowing frontier AI development; his data center remarks concern electricity costs, not risks from AI itself.

pause.note: No statement found for or against a pause on frontier AI development.

intl.note: No statement found on coordinating with China on the pace of AI development; he is not among the signers of the 23 September 2026 letter.
sources: Van Hollen press release listing the signers

rsi.note: No statement found on a ban on self-improving AI.

record: Voted on 1 October 2026 to advance the Ratepayer Protection Act (data centers of 100 megawatts or more to pay their own grid costs); the cloture vote failed 57-43.
Introduced a bipartisan homelessness bill whose summary says it supports better use of data, including artificial intelligence tools, to direct resources.
grade_reason: The only statement about AI found since 1 January 2025 is about staying competitive in AI and who pays for data center electricity. Nothing found acknowledges or dismisses catastrophic risk from AI.
notes: Seven web searches ran; none was refused. No statement by Crapo on superintelligence, extinction, loss of control, bioweapons, AI safety, a pause, or a China agreement was found. He did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter (not on the verified signer list). No source found shows him co-sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (reported sponsors are Sanders and Casar); the official co-sponsor list on congress.gov was not checked. Older AI material on his site is outside the date range and not included as statements: a 9 November 2023 Crapo-Wyden letter to federal agencies on their AI use, a 2024 Finance Committee hearing statement on AI in health care, and a 7 August 2024 Crapo-Wyden letter on AI safeguards at the Social Security Administration; all concern government use of AI, not catastrophic risk. Pages opened: the Ratepayer Protection Act release (wording read directly from the page), the homelessness bill release, and the 2023 and 2024 letters (read through a summarising fetch tool). Hearing transcripts and floor speeches were not searched separately, so remarks there could have been missed.
